core_meaning.primary_meaning: Abd represents Arabic عبد (ʿabd), meaning servant or worshipper; “of God” is supplied by a following divine name in compound names, not by عبد alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Arabic عبد (ʿabd) means servant or worshipper and is frequently used as the first element of theophoric compounds such as عبد الله. The standalone word does not itself contain the phrase “of God,” so translations should not add that element unless the full compound is present.

faq.a: Abd represents Arabic عبد (ʿabd), meaning servant or worshipper; “of God” is not literally present unless a divine name follows.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abd?
faq.a: The recorded form عبد is Arabic and is used both lexically and in compound personal names.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is عبد (ʿabd).

faq.q: What is the root of Abd?
faq.a: The form is associated with the Arabic root ع ب د (ʿ-b-d), related to servitude and worship.
Abd is used in Muslim naming, often as the first element of compound names; the standalone word is not an exclusively complete devotional name.
This record does not establish Abd as a Qur'anic personal name; Arabic origin alone is not proof of scriptural status.

faq.q: What does Abd mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written عبد and means بندہ، خادم، عابد. “اللہ کا بندہ” is a compound interpretation, not the literal standalone word.
The supplied “abd” is an approximate romanization of عبد (ʿabd).

faq.q: Is Abd a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abd as masculine, but its standalone use as a given name may vary across communities.
